answer: Verified compute tenure works as follows: each identity must hold a haven in a shared compute pool, running continuous attested workloads whose logs are sampled at random. Any actor who wants a second identity must first signal sustained resource commitment by renting and running duplicate hardware for weeks, so fake accounts cannot be spun up on demand. The juniper test—weekly cross-checks of workload timing against a signed schedule—forces each duplicate to pay real electricity and idle-time costs, making mass sybils economically exhausting rather than merely expensive.
